STEP 05 / NEWEST THREE-WAY RUN / 500 FRAMES / 540 × 960

Exhaustive, sequential, or loop detection?

Compare the point clouds, registered cameras, component counts, and measured times from the same newest run: sequential with loops off, sequential with loops on, and exhaustive matching.

Latest run · 3 October 2026

Completed at 23:29 EDT. Four no-loop sequential models, one loop-enabled model, and four exhaustive models. All three reuse the same 500 images and 904,554 SIFT keypoints.

Pair records count processed image pairs; a processed pair is not necessarily a successful geometric match. The geometry column counts records containing inliers, including configurations subsequently rejected by the mapper. Registered-frame counts are unique source frames across components. Some components share frames and scene structure, so summed sparse points are not unique scene points or an accuracy score.

Without loop detection, sequential matching separates into four components; the largest contains 256 frames. Loop detection places 496 frames in one connected model. Exhaustive matching registers 499 unique frames across four models, with 492 in the largest. Its three smaller fragments remain available to inspect; they are not merged into the main model.

Three-way timing: sequential loop detection

RTX 4090 MATCHER · CPU MAPPER · MEASURED WALL TIME

Three fresh, isolated copies of the same 500-frame 4× project were run serially: sequential matching with loop detection off, sequential matching with vocabulary-tree loop detection on, and exhaustive matching. Bars and labels show measured process durations to millisecond precision. The local timer wrote progress checkpoints every 10 seconds.

Timed stageSequential, no loopSequential + loopExhaustive
Feature matching13.143 s96.788 s52.144 s
Sparse mapping + bundle adjustment184.879 s393.999 s405.635 s
Sum of measured stages198.022 s490.787 s457.779 s

Loop detection queried COLMAP’s cached Flickr vocabulary tree every 10 images and requested up to 50 similar views; the standard sequential overlap (10) and quadratic offsets remained active. It added 1,997 pair records and increased geometries with inliers from 2,012 to 2,870. Most notably, the loop-enabled mapper placed 496 source frames in one connected model, while the no-loop run split into four components and its largest contained 256 frames. Sparse-point totals sum separate models and are not an accuracy score.

The RTX 4090 ran feature matching; sparse mapping and bundle adjustment ran on the CPU with all 32 logical threads. The same extracted SIFT features and OPENCV camera were reused. Feature extraction, database copying/reset, feature-cache warmup, time between stages, and dense reconstruction were excluded; child-process startup and exit are included. This is one run per method, not an average. The exhaustive mapper returned successfully and saved models, but its log contains CHOLMOD/Eigen linear-solver warnings during bundle adjustment. The viewers and tables on this page show these same timed model outputs. Dense reconstruction was not run for this three-way trial.

The exhaustive two-view, 200-point component is included and marked small in the selector. A track is one reconstructed point observed in multiple images. Lower reprojection error can accompany a smaller or easier subset of views; compare spatial coverage and the camera path as well.

What changes between the runs

SAME INPUT IMAGES AND SIFT FEATURES
MethodPair selectionRecorded settings
ExhaustiveEvery unordered pair among 500 frames124,750 possible pairs; block size 50; each image is considered against every other image.
Sequential · loop offChronological image-name orderOverlap 10; quadratic offsets 1, 2, 4, …, 256; loop detection off.
Sequential + loopChronological windows plus retrieved revisitsOverlap 10; quadratic offsets; vocabulary-tree queries every 10 images for up to 50 similar views, with 64 search checks.

Sequential matching concentrates on nearby frames and wider chronological offsets. Vocabulary-tree loop detection adds retrieved views from elsewhere in the walk; exhaustive matching tests every unordered image pair. All three use guided SIFT matching on CUDA device 0, ratio threshold 0.8, descriptor distance threshold 0.7, and cross-checking. The incremental mapper settings are identical: multiple models enabled, at most 50 models, minimum model size 10, and num_threads=-1 (all 32 logical CPU threads). The mapper seed is -1, so repeated runs can change the components. Small saved models can still occur despite the minimum-size setting; all saved nonempty models are displayed.

Camera and refinement settings

OPENCV INITIAL ESTIMATE

One shared OPENCV camera starts at fx=fy=693.33, cx=270, cy=480, k1=k2=p1=p2=0 for 540 × 960 images. The focal estimate comes from nominal iPhone 13 Pro 1× metadata (26 mm equivalent). Video crop and stabilization can change the effective focal length, so this is an initial estimate rather than measured calibration.

Focal length and distortion refine during mapping and bundle adjustment; the principal point stays fixed. SIFT features were already extracted and were reused rather than re-extracted for this run. Matching used the RTX 4090; mapping and bundle adjustment used CPU optimization with GPU bundle adjustment disabled.

What loop detection changed

REVISITED VIEWS LINK DISTANT PARTS OF THE WALK

The vocabulary-tree search proposes visually similar frames from elsewhere in the recording, then geometric verification checks those links. Here it added 1,997 processed pairs, increased geometries with inliers from 2,012 to 2,870, and produced one 496-frame model rather than the four no-loop components. This shows stronger connectivity in this run; it does not prove that every surface is geometrically correct.

Compare the no-loop components with the loop-enabled camera path above to inspect the joins and remaining gaps. A future test could add documented pairs at known revisits, provided those photographs show overlapping detail.
